citations.citation: For the invention and development of the optical lattice clock, in which atoms trapped at a magic wavelength are interrogated by the thousands without Doppler or recoil shifts, bringing optical clocks to uncertainties near one part in 10^18

For the invention and development of the optical lattice clock, in which atoms are trapped at a magic wavelength so that many of them can be interrogated without Doppler, recoil or light-shift perturbation, bringing optical clocks to uncertainties near one part in 10^18

For the invention and realisation of the optical lattice clock, in which atoms trapped at a magic wavelength are interrogated in large numbers free of Doppler and recoil shifts, bringing optical clocks to uncertainties near one part in 10^18

for the invention and development of the optical lattice clock, in which atoms trapped at a magic wavelength are interrogated without Doppler, recoil or light-shift perturbation, bringing frequency measurement to uncertainties near 1e-18

for the invention and development of the optical lattice clock, in which many neutral atoms are trapped at a magic wavelength so that the clock transition is unperturbed, bringing atomic timekeeping to the 10^-18 level

For the invention and development of the optical lattice clock, in which atoms are held at a magic wavelength so that many neutral atoms are interrogated without Doppler or recoil shifts, reaching fractional uncertainties near one part in 10^18

for the invention and realisation of the optical lattice clock, in which atoms trapped at a magic wavelength are interrogated free of Doppler and recoil shifts, and for bringing it to a fractional uncertainty near 1e-18

for the invention and development of the optical lattice clock, in which atoms held at a magic wavelength are interrogated by the thousand without Doppler or recoil shifts, bringing atomic time keeping to the 10^-18 level
